hook.line: How are you supposed to get marketing experience when every job already requires some?
hook.visual: Close selfie framing at a desk; at 0.75 s three photo stickers pop in (marketing word collage, woman with binders, office) then vanish at the first cut.

beats.what: Opens mid-question, eyes to camera, word-by-word caption in the middle
Photo cutouts stack in one by one over her face to illustrate 'marketing experience'
Cut back to clean face, then the promise: five ways to get experience
Tip one: make your own fake campaign for a brand
Tip two: early-career organisations and events
Tip three: online courses for the fundamentals
Zoom punch on 'Use LinkedIn' as she repeats it, a running joke
Last tip: network, e.g. free events on Eventbrite
Wrap-up: create the opportunities you want
Sign-off 'happy marketing', then the TikTok end card

why_it_works: The opening question names a catch-22 every beginner feels, so the target viewer self-selects in the first 3 s
A numbered promise ('five ways') gives viewers a reason to stay to the end
Personal proof (two work placements she got) makes generic advice credible
The repeated 'use LinkedIn' line becomes a callback joke she acknowledges, which feels human
weaknesses: 160 s with one long take and almost no visual change after the hook
The promised list has no on-screen numbers, so viewers lose track of which tip they are on
Music bed sits close to the voice (-13.1 dB bed vs -11.6 LUFS)
No call to action at all
for_robert: Use the hook trick: pop two or three pictures over his face in the first second to illustrate the question, then clear them. Avoid her long single take; put each tip's number on screen.
